findings.text: _cold_build publishes the unpatched build through _store_cold_build at :635 and only then takes the marks at :636, so a second reader entering index_rows in that window reads the cached build and _absorb_marked at :689 pops the marks the path was meant to consume; the path then pops nothing and returns rows read before a change recorded while it ran, which is the clause the section adds, and if that concurrent _absorb_marked returns None the marks are gone while the cache keeps the unpatched build. Popping the marks before publishing the build closes the window.

the delivered negative control arms all seven mutations in one pytest run (logs/negative-control-cold-read.log:4), so the log shows seven failures but cannot attribute each to its own case: a mutation that also reddened a second case's test would read identically in the same seven-id list, and the done-when asks for each control to be applied and logged with its failing test id. The run's later attempt has since written one log per mutation (logs/negative-control-RECKON_TEST_COLD_*.log), which is the evidence shape this finding asks for.

the log named by the manifest's tests: line and by its checkpoint ('gate 203 passed EXIT=0 at d8ecab5e0') now carries '# revision: ebf3c554ec6a' and ends after its '# command:' header with no pytest summary and no EXIT= line, so a later reader cannot read the recorded combined-gate result from the artefact it is told to open and the done-when's 'every log ends in EXIT=' clause is not met at that path; the run's concurrent second attempt re-ran the same command over the same file at 09:31Z.
